title: Choosing Context: Selection, Ordering and Compression
summary: The context window is a budget shared by instructions, history, tools, documents and the answer. This lesson treats it like one: what to include, where to put it so the model actually uses it, and how far you can compress before facts are lost.
objectives: Write a context budget equation and compute how many retrieved chunks fit after fixed costs and the output reserve
Select context under a token budget by relevance per token, and explain when greedy selection is suboptimal
Describe the lost-in-the-middle effect and compute expected recall for a given ordering of documents
Order context to maximise expected use of the relevant parts, using the rearrangement argument
Estimate how much information survives compression and when more context costs more than it helps
prerequisites: You should know how prompts are rendered and priced from [Anatomy of a Prompt](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-anatomy) and what a context window and prefill are from [Context windows, prefill and the KV cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache). Retrieval itself is covered in module 6; here we take a ranked list of candidate passages as given.
